_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The copied edit command of a personal integration keeps its SSH arguments intact. The VM has one personal integration, gh (GitHub). The page's clipboard is a fake that tells the server what was copied. Call "ssh args" runs the copied command in sh with ssh defined as a function that prints its arguments, and returns them as a JSON array (each NUL-terminated, so the list ends with ""); call "edit args" does the same with the second of those arguments, run as a command with integrations defined that way ("none" before anything was copied). Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does; "named X" means an exact name match. "The modal" is ".integrations-modal". To "open the panel": press Control+k; ".command-palette-input" should be visible; fill it with "integration", click the first ".command-palette-item", and the modal should be visible. To "select" an integration N: click the first ".integrations-tabs button" (the list), then the ".integrations-name-btn" whose text starts with N followed by a space; ".integrations-detail-head strong" should then have exactly the text N. "The refresh button" is the modal's button named "Refresh"; "the Slack test button" is the button named "Test integration (webhook only)"; "the notify button" is the button named "Send test notification". To "close the modal": click the modal's button whose name contains "Close modal". To "start": navigate to /new, wait for the element with data-testid "message-input" to be visible, and open the panel. Perform the steps in order. 1. Start, and select gh. 2. Click ".integrations-advanced summary", then the button named "Copy edit command". The button inside the second ".integrations-copy-line" should have exactly the text "Copied". 3. Call "ssh args": it must return ["exe.dev","integrations edit 'gh' --comment='<new comment>'",""]. 4. Call "edit args": it must return ["edit","gh","--comment=<new comment>",""].
